File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: Line 16935 — `cp "${JUDGE_PROMPT_FILE}" "${judge_attempt_prompt_file}"`
Problem: The judge retry loop performs an unguarded `cp` under `set -e -u -o pipefail`. The reviewer path in `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` correctly guards its equivalent `cp` at line 3164 with `if cp ... 2>/dev/null; then ... else ...`, and falls back to the base prompt file on failure. The judge path has no such guard.
Why it fails at runtime: Under `set -e`, a non-zero exit from `cp` terminates the poller shell process immediately. A transient filesystem issue (disk full, permission error, I/O error) would kill the entire orchestrate-poll cycle rather than falling back to the original prompt file as the fail-open nag-reminder contract intends.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
Line or code reference: Line 1783 — `cp "${EDITOR_PROMPT_FILE}" "${attempt_prompt_file}"`
Problem: Same unguarded `cp` pattern as the judge path. The reviewer path in `review_run_reviewers.sh` correctly guards its equivalent `cp` but the editor path was not given the same treatment.
Why it fails at runtime: Under `set -e`, a `cp` failure aborts the script before the editor's own retry loop can recover. The editor has `editor_max_attempts=3`, but if `cp` fails on attempt 1, the process exits before attempting 2 or 3.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

The counter would then fail to accumulate silent rounds, preventing nag reminders from triggering when they should.

File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: Line 16936 — `cp "${JUDGE_PROMPT_FILE}" "${judge_attempt_prompt_file}"`
Problem: The judge retry loop performs an unguarded `cp` under `set -euo pipefail` (established in line 1). A transient filesystem failure at this call site terminates the entire poller process immediately, bypassing all remaining poller logic for every project tracked by that tick. The equivalent reviewer path in `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:3164` correctly guards the same pattern with `if cp ... 2>/dev/null; then ... else` and falls back to the base prompt file with a warning. This judge path has no such guard.
Why it fails at runtime: Under `set -e`, any non-zero exit from `cp` (disk full, permission error, transient IO error) kills the shell before the retry loop, fallback logic, or fail-open nag contract can execute. The orchestrator poller should continue with `${JUDGE_PROMPT_FILE}` as the effective prompt when the copy cannot be created — identical to the reviewer pattern.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: Line 16935-16940 (judge retry loop nag injection path)
Problem: The nag-reminder injection is designed as fail-open, but the unguarded `cp` in the same path makes the entire orchestrator poller fail-closed on transient IO errors. This creates a declared-vs-effective capability gap: the `UNATTENDED_NAG_REMINDER_ENABLED=false` default and fail-open contract are bypassed by a crash in the injection plumbing.
Why it fails at runtime: Even when the operator has `UNATTENDED_NAG_REMINDER_ENABLED=false` (the default), the `cp` call still executes regardless of whether a nag block will be produced, so the crash path is active even for operators who have the feature disabled entirely.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
